title: test-0112-SOC-ECO-CONSUMER
passage: Consumer exploitation is not limited to any specific social or economic group; even highly educated individuals can be deceived by sophisticated marketing or hidden product defects. Sellers may use unfair trade practices regardless of the store's reputation, as even premium branded outlets can sometimes sell adulterated or substandard goods. To protect themselves, consumers must rely on official certification marks rather than brand names alone. For instance, the ISI mark is used for industrial and electrical goods to ensure safety standards, while the Agmark is specifically reserved for agricultural and food products. When a consumer faces exploitation, they do not need to approach the highest judicial body immediately. Instead, the Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) has established a three-tier quasi-judicial machinery at the district, state, and national levels. A consumer can file a complaint at the District Forum for claims up to twenty lakh rupees, ensuring that justice is accessible and local. By understanding these rights and the proper certification marks, every buyer can make informed choices and seek redressal effectively. It is essential to remember that awareness is the primary tool against exploitation, regardless of one's background or the store's status. Always check for the correct certification mark before purchasing any item to ensure you are getting exactly what you paid for.
summary: Consumer exploitation is not limited to any specific social or economic group — even highly educated people can be deceived by sophisticated marketing or hidden product defects. To protect themselves, consumers should use official certification marks instead of just brand names.
